facts.subject: random
facts.title: Dancing plague of 1518
facts.text: In July 1518 in Strasbourg, a woman reportedly began dancing in the street, and dozens to hundreds of others joined over the following weeks. The cause is still debated: ergot poisoning has been proposed, but mass psychogenic illness is the more popular theory.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Emu War
facts.text: In late 1932 the Australian army sent soldiers with Lewis guns to Western Australia's Campion district to cull emus damaging crops. The emus scattered into small groups and the effort was widely seen as a failure; the commander's claim of 986 kills is disputed as inflated.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Cadaver Synod
facts.text: In January 897, Pope Stephen VI had the exhumed corpse of Pope Formosus put on trial in Rome, propped on a throne with a deacon answering for it. Formosus was found guilty, but after Stephen was deposed, later popes annulled the verdict.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Mpemba effect
facts.text: The Mpemba effect is the claim that hotter liquid can freeze faster than colder liquid. It is named for Tanzanian student Erasto Mpemba, who noticed it with ice cream mix in 1963; whether it reliably occurs in water is still debated.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Turritopsis dohrnii
facts.text: Turritopsis dohrnii, a jellyfish whose bell is only about 4.5 mm wide, can revert from adult medusa back to a polyp by transdifferentiation, so it is called biologically immortal. It can still be eaten or die of disease, and reversion has not been seen in the wild.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Wow! signal
facts.text: On 15 August 1977, Ohio State's Big Ear telescope recorded a 72-second narrowband radio signal near the hydrogen line frequency. Astronomer Jerry Ehman wrote 'Wow!' beside it. It has never been detected again, and its origin remains unexplained.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Pitch drop experiment
facts.text: In 1927 Thomas Parnell set pitch dripping through a funnel at the University of Queensland. Pitch is estimated to be roughly 230 billion times as viscous as water, so only nine drops have fallen there in decades, and several fell when nobody was watching.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Tunguska event
facts.text: On 30 June 1908 an explosion over Siberia flattened about 2,150 km² of forest, yet no impact crater was found. Most scientists favor an asteroid air burst, but no fragment has been formally identified and the asteroid-versus-comet question is still debated.

facts.subject: cardiology
facts.title: Werner Forßmann
facts.text: According to the usual account, in 1929 German physician Werner Forßmann passed a urinary catheter through a vein in his own arm and went to the X-ray department to confirm it had reached his heart, about 60 cm in. He shared the 1956 Nobel Prize for the technique's development.

facts.subject: cardiology
facts.title: Voodoo death
facts.text: Physiologist Walter Cannon proposed in 1942 that intense fear, such as of a curse, could cause sudden death by overdriving the sympathetic-adrenal system. Later researchers disagree on the mechanism; Curt Richter's rat studies pointed instead to vagal overactivity and hopelessness.

facts.subject: cardiology
facts.title: Channichthyidae
facts.text: Antarctic crocodile icefish are among the few adult vertebrates with no hemoglobin, so their blood is colorless and carries oxygen dissolved in plasma. They compensate with larger hearts, about four times the blood volume of other fish and roughly five times the cardiac output.

facts.subject: cardiology
facts.title: Diving reflex
facts.text: Cold water on the face during a breath-hold triggers the diving reflex: heart rate drops by roughly 10 to 25 percent and limb blood vessels constrict, directing blood toward the heart, brain and lungs. Infants up to about six months old show a strong response.

facts.subject: medicine
facts.title: Fatal insomnia
facts.text: Fatal familial insomnia is an inherited prion disease caused by a D178N mutation in the PRNP gene, which degenerates the thalamus. Patients lose the ability to sleep and typically die 6 to 36 months after onset, which usually begins around age 50.

facts.subject: medicine
facts.title: Alien hand syndrome
facts.text: In alien hand syndrome, a limb moves purposefully but outside the person's control, most often the left hand after damage to the corpus callosum or frontal lobe. Kurt Goldstein published the first case in 1908, and Peter Sellers's character in Dr. Strangelove is often cited as portraying it.

facts.subject: medicine
facts.title: Lazarus phenomenon
facts.text: The Lazarus phenomenon is the spontaneous return of a heartbeat after someone has been pronounced dead, called autoresuscitation when it follows failed CPR. It is extremely rare and poorly understood; one hypothesis is that chest pressure built up during CPR is involved.

facts.subject: medicine
facts.title: Foreign accent syndrome
facts.text: In foreign accent syndrome, usually after a stroke, a person's speech begins to sound foreign to listeners even though they never learned that accent. Pierre Marie described it in 1907. It stems from disrupted speech planning and muscle coordination, not from acquiring a real accent.

facts.subject: spanish
facts.title: La Tomatina
facts.text: La Tomatina es una batalla de tomates que se celebra en Buñol, Valencia, el último miércoles de agosto. Dura una hora y se usan casi 150 toneladas de tomates. Su origen no está del todo claro, pero la versión más fiable dice que empezó en 1945.
facts.translation: La Tomatina is a tomato fight held in Buñol, Valencia, on the last Wednesday of August. It lasts one hour and uses almost 150 tons of tomatoes. Its origin is not fully clear, but the most reliable version says it began in 1945.

facts.subject: spanish
facts.title: Relámpago del Catatumbo
facts.text: El Relámpago del Catatumbo es una tormenta eléctrica casi constante sobre el lago de Maracaibo, en Venezuela. Puede durar hasta diez horas por noche. Los científicos todavía no se ponen de acuerdo sobre su causa.
facts.translation: The Catatumbo lightning is an almost constant electrical storm over Lake Maracaibo, in Venezuela. It can last up to ten hours a night. Scientists still do not agree on its cause.

facts.subject: mandarin
facts.title: 臭豆腐
facts.text: 臭豆腐是发酵的豆腐，味道很臭，很多人把它炸熟后当小吃。
facts.translation: Stinky tofu is fermented tofu with a very strong smell, and many people fry it and eat it as a snack.
facts.reading: Chòu dòufu shì fājiào de dòufu, wèidào hěn chòu, hěn duō rén bǎ tā zhá shú hòu dàng xiǎochī.

facts.subject: mandarin
facts.title: 月牙泉
facts.text: 月牙泉在甘肃敦煌的沙漠里，形状像月亮，最长约一百五十米。
facts.translation: Crescent Lake is in the desert at Dunhuang, Gansu. It is shaped like a moon and is about 150 meters long at most.
facts.reading: Yuèyáquán zài Gānsù Dūnhuáng de shāmò lǐ, xíngzhuàng xiàng yuèliang, zuì cháng yuē yībǎi wǔshí mǐ.
